top_needs.title: Braces treatment outcomes and efficiency improvements with DM monitoring
top_needs.brands_and_products: No specific brands — general orthodontic appliances
top_needs.metrics_sought: treatment duration in months, emergency visit frequency, percentage of on-track cases, patient compliance rate, chair time per appointment
top_needs.doctor_objections: Orthodontists often believe traditional in-office braces monitoring is sufficient and doubt that remote monitoring can reduce treatment time or emergencies. They worry DM might add complexity without clear efficiency gains or improved patient outcomes.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: peer-reviewed retrospective cohort studies comparing treatment duration and emergency rates, case series demonstrating compliance improvements, expert opinion/KOL testimonials on workflow impact
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a lack of robust comparative studies quantifying how DM remote monitoring specifically shortens braces treatment time and reduces emergency visits. Prioritize creating controlled cohort studies with clear efficiency and outcome metrics.

top_needs.title: Practice workflow optimization and efficiency gains using DM remote monitoring
top_needs.brands_and_products: No specific brands — general orthodontic appliances
top_needs.metrics_sought: chair time saved per appointment, number of appointments reduced per patient, staff time saved, patient no-show rate, overall practice throughput
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question whether DM actually reduces chair time or appointment frequency, fearing it may increase workload reviewing scans. Some doubt if DM integrates smoothly into existing workflows without disruption.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: white papers with practice data on time savings, ROI calculators, workflow case studies, peer-reviewed observational studies on appointment frequency changes
top_needs.gap_assessment: Missing are detailed practice-level data and ROI analyses showing concrete time and cost savings from DM integration. Developing practice workflow case studies and ROI tools would address this gap.

top_needs.title: DM AI tooth movement detection accuracy versus in-person clinical assessment
top_needs.brands_and_products: No specific brands — general orthodontic appliances
top_needs.metrics_sought: AI detection accuracy percentage, sensitivity and specificity rates, false positive/negative rates, agreement rate with clinician assessments
top_needs.doctor_objections: Clinicians doubt AI can match their diagnostic accuracy and worry about false alerts or missed issues. They question if AI can reliably replace or supplement their clinical judgment.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: product accuracy validation studies, peer-reviewed diagnostic accuracy studies, regulatory clearance documentation, expert KOL testimonials
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a need for more published validation studies comparing DM AI accuracy directly to clinician assessments in real-world settings. Prioritize rigorous diagnostic accuracy research and regulatory evidence.

top_needs.title: Clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction with aligner treatment monitored by DM
top_needs.metrics_sought: treatment duration, patient compliance rates, patient satisfaction scores, number of refinements needed, percentage of on-track cases
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question if DM monitoring improves aligner compliance or reduces treatment time compared to standard recall visits. Some doubt patient satisfaction gains are significant.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: RCTs or cohort studies comparing DM-monitored vs standard aligner treatment, patient satisfaction surveys, before/after case galleries
top_needs.gap_assessment: Limited RCTs exist showing DM’s impact on aligner treatment efficiency and patient satisfaction. Creating controlled comparative studies and patient-reported outcome data is a priority.

top_needs.title: SmartSTL digital impression accuracy and clinical utility compared to traditional impressions
top_needs.metrics_sought: impression accuracy rates, time to capture impressions, patient comfort scores, reduction in retakes, integration with treatment planning
top_needs.doctor_objections: Clinicians are skeptical if SmartSTL scans match the accuracy of traditional impressions and whether it truly saves chair time or improves patient comfort.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: validation studies comparing SmartSTL to traditional impressions, case series demonstrating clinical workflow integration, patient comfort surveys
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a shortage of head-to-head accuracy and workflow studies for SmartSTL versus traditional impressions. Prioritize clinical validation and patient experience research.

top_needs.title: Retention phase monitoring effectiveness and relapse prevention with DM
top_needs.brands_and_products: No specific brands — general orthodontic appliances
top_needs.metrics_sought: relapse rates, retention compliance rates, frequency of retention adjustments, patient satisfaction during retention
top_needs.doctor_objections: Orthodontists doubt if remote monitoring during retention reduces relapse or improves compliance compared to standard recall visits. Some see retention as low priority for remote monitoring.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: retrospective cohort studies on relapse rates with DM, patient compliance surveys, expert opinion articles on retention monitoring
top_needs.gap_assessment: Evidence on DM’s impact on retention compliance and relapse prevention is sparse. Developing longitudinal studies focused on retention phase outcomes is needed.

top_needs.title: Patient experience and satisfaction improvements using DM remote monitoring
top_needs.brands_and_products: No specific brands — general orthodontic appliances
top_needs.metrics_sought: patient satisfaction scores, perceived convenience, anxiety reduction, engagement rates, no-show rates
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question if patients truly prefer remote monitoring or if it adds complexity. Some doubt it improves patient engagement or reduces no-shows.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: patient satisfaction surveys, qualitative studies on patient experience, case studies highlighting engagement improvements
top_needs.gap_assessment: More patient-centered research quantifying satisfaction and engagement benefits of DM is needed. Prioritize patient survey data and qualitative feedback studies.

top_needs.title: Engage app impact on patient compliance and treatment outcomes
top_needs.metrics_sought: patient compliance rates, treatment adherence, app usage statistics, treatment outcome improvements
top_needs.doctor_objections: Clinicians doubt if the Engage app meaningfully improves compliance or if patients consistently use it. Some see it as a gimmick without clinical benefit.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: usage analytics reports, cohort studies linking app use to compliance, expert testimonials
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is limited published data correlating Engage app usage with improved compliance and outcomes. Prioritize analytics and clinical correlation studies.

top_needs.title: Hygiene monitoring and oral health outcomes with DM remote check-ins
top_needs.brands_and_products: No specific brands — general orthodontic appliances
top_needs.metrics_sought: oral hygiene scores, incidence of gingivitis or caries, patient compliance with hygiene instructions
top_needs.doctor_objections: Doctors question if remote monitoring can effectively track hygiene or improve oral health compared to in-office checks. Some doubt patient adherence to hygiene advice remotely.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: clinical observational studies on hygiene outcomes, patient compliance surveys, expert opinion articles
top_needs.gap_assessment: Few studies document hygiene improvements attributable to DM monitoring. Developing clinical outcome studies focused on oral health metrics is needed.

top_needs.title: Phase 1 orthodontic treatment monitoring effectiveness with DM
top_needs.brands_and_products: No specific brands — general orthodontic appliances
top_needs.metrics_sought: treatment progress tracking accuracy, treatment duration, patient compliance, early intervention rates
top_needs.doctor_objections: Orthodontists are unsure if DM adds value in Phase 1 treatment, which often requires frequent in-person adjustments. They question if remote monitoring can detect issues early enough.
top_needs.evidence_type_needed: case series on Phase 1 treatment with DM, expert opinion articles, observational studies on early intervention rates
top_needs.gap_assessment: There is a lack of focused evidence on DM’s role in Phase 1 treatment monitoring. Prioritize case studies and expert consensus on early treatment phases.
